cues.zh: 我们不必处理的 JavaScriptSo, I'm going to talk about maybe something that is somewhat unusual.I normally am a Rust developer.And I work on rust-analyzer, which is an IDE backend for Rust.But sometimes I write JavaScript.And the thing is, every time I write JavaScript, I try to see how much Rust can I get into the JavaScript.And today I want to talk about a project that is a result of this.It's called dprint. It's a code formatter.But before I get to the actual, like, what it is, I want to talk about the setup that brought us here.So, yeah, let's go.So, my main job is working on rust-analyzer.And rust-analyzer is a pretty big codebase, and it's written in Rust.And the problem with IDEs is that they are not just compilers.Compilers are mostly batch programs.You feed them input, they produce output, they terminate.Ideally, they should be fast, but it's fine if they're not, because you only run them once in a while.But IDEs are different.IDEs are interactive.They should respond to user input in real time.And the problem with IDEs is that they need to maintain a lot of state.And the state is constantly changing.So, the architecture of IDEs is much more about state management than the architecture of compilers.And this is where the Rust part comes in.Rust is really good at managing state.It has a lot of tools for that: ownership, borrow checking, and so on.But Rust is not really good at being fast and interactive at the same time.Well, actually it is, but it's complicated.And this is kind of the tension that we have in rust-analyzer.So, what does this have to do with JavaScript?Well, the thing is that the IDE that we are building is not just the backend.It's also the frontend.And the frontend is where the user interacts with the IDE.And the frontend is usually written in JavaScript.So, we have this split: the backend is in Rust, the frontend is in JavaScript.And the communication between them is a problem.Because the backend and the frontend are written in different languages, they have different runtimes, different memory models, and so on.So, we need some kind of protocol to communicate between them.And this protocol is usually based on JSON.And this is where the performance problems start.Because JSON is not a very efficient format.And the backend and the frontend are constantly communicating.So, the question is: how can we make this communication faster?And this is where the idea of not using JavaScript comes in.So, the idea is: what if we write the frontend in Rust as well?And compile it to WebAssembly.Then we can have the same language, the same runtime, and the same memory model on both sides.And we can avoid the JSON serialization and deserialization.And this is what we did with dprint.So, dprint is a code formatter written in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly, and running in the browser.And it's fast.Thank you.
